name: Avarua
tagline: The capital, on the ring road at the north
description: Rarotonga's town, a short strip on the northern side of the ring road with the banks, the Punanga Nui market, the post office and the harbour. It is the only place on the island that functions as a town and it is quiet.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, the market and the island's services
pros: Punanga Nui market on Saturday mornings
cons: The beach here is not the island's best

name: Muri
description: The eastern side of the island, where the lagoon widens over pale sand with four small motu offshore, and the water is calm enough to paddle across. Most of the island's accommodation, restaurants and the night market are here.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is the lagoon and being near restaurants
pros: The finest lagoon on the island
Most restaurants and the Muri night market
Paddleboarding and kayaking from the beach
cons: The most expensive part of Rarotonga
Seagrass in the shallows in places

name: Arorangi
tagline: The western side, for the sunsets
description: The district on the western coast, facing the sunset, with a string of small resorts and self-catering places along the road and the Cook Islands Christian Church at its centre, one of the oldest buildings on the island.
bestFor: Anyone who wants sunsets and a quieter stretch of coast
cons: The lagoon is narrower on this side
Reef passages here have strong currents

name: The Inland Valleys
tagline: Behind the ring road, into the mountains
description: The mountainous interior of Rarotonga, uninhabited and crossed by the Cross-Island Track that passes the volcanic plug called the Needle, with valleys of taro and banana running up from the coastal road on every side.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the walk across the island
pros: The Cross-Island Track and the Needle
cons: The track is muddy and steep
Everything else is on the coast

name: Aitutaki (265 km north by air)
tagline: The lagoon people mistake Rarotonga for
description: An island an hour north by air, with a lagoon that is genuinely among the most beautiful in the world, ringed by motu with One Foot Island at its southern edge. It is smaller, flatter and quieter than Rarotonga.
bestFor: Anyone who came for the postcard lagoon
pros: One of the world's great lagoons
One Foot Island and the motu
cons: A separate island and a flight away
